request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the

agent.result_text:
Sheets in the same tree now share one number sequence. When a claim is opened, it gets the number after the highest one given on any sheet in the tree. Numbers already given don't change, and per-period numbering is still counted per sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests; after that I only re-wrapped a comment and checked that the code still compiles.

What changed:
- **`Claims.nextNumber`** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/Claims.java`) now takes the sheet plus the other sheets in its tree. It finds the highest last number across all of them, adds one, and saves that as the opening sheet's last number. It locks every counter row in the tree while it does this, so two claims opened at the same moment on different sheets can't get the same number. No database change was needed: the existing per-sheet counter table is enough.
- **`Settings.wholeTree`** (new) walks up the parents to the top sheet and returns it with everything below it.
- **`ClaimStatusChanger.number`** uses the shared sequence. Everything else that numbers claims goes through this method too — opening, splitting, reassigning, cloning a sheet and transferring a person — so they all follow the new rule.

**Decision for you:** I applied the shared sequence to the whole connected tree, which includes sibling sheets (two children of the same parent). That differs from the app's existing "tree" used for name clashes, which covers only a sheet's ancestors and descendants, so siblings don't count there. I chose the wider version because if siblings didn't share, numbers in one tree could repeat. The test never checks siblings, so if you want it to match the narrower meaning, it's a one-line switch to `settings.tree(sheet)` in `ClaimStatusChanger`.
